title: Subdivision 124-B roll-over — asset compulsorily acquired, lost or destroyed
summary: Replacement-asset roll-over where a CGT asset is compulsorily acquired by a government agency (or under a covered law), lost or destroyed, or disposed of after an acquisition notice. You must receive money or another CGT asset as compensation and, for money, acquire a replacement asset or repair the original within the time limits (1 year before / 1 year after the income year). The gain is reduced or disregarded and the replacement asset inherits the original's cost base. Subsection coverage: operative sections 124-70, 124-75, 124-80, 124-85, 124-90, 124-95, 103-25 mapped to nodes; 103-25 (machinery).

nodes.label: You own a CGT asset and it is compulsorily acquired, lost or destroyed (or disposed of under threat of acquisition)
nodes.body: Subdivision 124-B lets you choose a roll-over where a CGT asset is compulsorily acquired, lost or destroyed and you receive money or another CGT asset as compensation, deferring the gain into a replacement asset.

nodes.label: A qualifying event happens to the original asset (s 124-70)
nodes.body: s 124-70(1): (a) compulsorily acquired by an Australian government agency; (aa) compulsorily acquired by another entity under a power conferred by a law covered by s 124-70(1A) (an Australian law other than Ch 6A Corps Act, or a corresponding foreign law); (b) lost or destroyed; (c) disposal to an entity (other than a foreign government agency) after a notice inviting negotiation and warning of compulsory acquisition, where the acquisition would have been under a s 124-70(1A) law; (ca)/(cb) land over which a mining lease was (or would have been) compulsorily granted and the lessee acquires it; (d) a lease granted by an Australian government agency expires and is not renewed. s 124-70(2): you must receive money or another CGT asset (except a car/motor cycle/similar vehicle), or both, as compensation or under an insurance policy.

nodes.label: Did you receive money or another CGT asset (not a car or similar vehicle) as compensation or under insurance?
nodes.body: You must receive money, another CGT asset (except a car, motor cycle or similar vehicle), or both, as compensation for the event or under an insurance policy against the risk of loss or destruction (s 124-70(2)). Further requirements apply for money (s 124-75) and for another asset (s 124-80).

rulings.title: Capital gains tax: Sale of shares without consent of owner

nodes.label: Do you make a capital gain from the event?
nodes.body: There are no roll-over consequences if you make a capital loss from the event (note to s 124-70). The roll-over only defers gains.

nodes.label: If you are a foreign resident (or foreign trust trustee) just after the event — is the replacement asset taxable Australian property?
nodes.body: Where the compensation includes another CGT asset, a foreign resident (or trustee of a foreign trust) can only get the roll-over if the replacement asset is taxable Australian property just after acquisition. This TAP requirement applies to the asset received — it does not apply where you receive only money.

nodes.label: Do you receive money, another CGT asset, or both?
nodes.body: Three branches: money only (s 124-75 requirements, then s 124-85 consequences); asset only (s 124-80 requirements, then s 124-90 consequences); both money and asset (s 124-95: requirements and consequences apply separately to each part — money part under s 124-75/124-85, asset part under s 124-80/124-90, with the s 124-95(2) proportional market-value requirement for the asset part).

nodes.label: Money case: do the s 124-75 requirements apply and are they satisfied?
nodes.body: s 124-75: (2) you must incur expenditure acquiring another CGT asset (not a Div 40/328 depreciating asset), or if part of the original asset is lost/destroyed, capital expenditure repairing/restoring it; (3) timing: at least some expenditure no earlier than 1 year before the event or later than 1 year after the end of the income year of the event (Commissioner may allow further time); (4) if the original asset was used/installed ready for use/being installed in your business just before the event, the other asset must be used in the business (or installed ready for use) for a reasonable time after acquisition — otherwise it must be used for the same/similar purpose as the original; (5) the other asset cannot become trading stock or a Div 40/328 depreciating asset just after acquisition; (6) cannot become a registered emissions unit.

nodes.label: Asset case: do the s 124-80 requirements apply and are they satisfied?
nodes.body: s 124-80: (2) the other asset cannot become trading stock, a Div 40/328 depreciating asset, or a registered emissions unit just after acquisition; (3) the market value of the other asset (when acquired) must exceed the cost base of the original asset just before the event.

nodes.label: Do you choose the roll-over (s 103-25)?
nodes.body: The roll-over applies only if you choose it (s 103-25: by the day you lodge your income tax return for the income year of the event, or within any further time the Commissioner allows). If you do not choose, the CGT event is taxed in full.

nodes.label: Money case consequences: gain reduced, not reduced or disregarded — and replacement expenditure reduced
nodes.body: For a post-CGT asset (s 124-85(2)): (1) if the money exceeds the replacement/repair expenditure and the gain is more than the excess, the gain is reduced to the excess and the expenditure is reduced accordingly; (2) if the gain is not more than the excess, the gain is not reduced; (3) if the money does not exceed the expenditure, the gain is disregarded and the expenditure is reduced by the gain. For a pre-CGT asset: the replacement asset is taken to be acquired before 20 September 1985 if the expenditure is not more than 120% of the original's market value, or a natural disaster made the replacement substantially the same; repairs keep pre-CGT status (s 124-85(3)-(4)).

rulings.title: for cost base purposes - to the extent to which it reflects a reduction in value of the…

nodes.label: Asset case consequences: gain disregarded; replacement's cost base is the original's cost base
nodes.body: The capital gain from the original asset is disregarded. For a post-CGT original asset, the first element of the other asset's cost base (and reduced cost base) is the original asset's cost base at the time of the event (s 124-90(2)-(3)). For a pre-CGT original asset, the other asset is taken to have been acquired before 20 September 1985 (s 124-90(4)).

nodes.label: Both money and asset: each part is treated separately with proportional attribution
nodes.body: s 124-95: each part of the compensation is treated separately. Money part: s 124-85 consequences (gain reduced, not reduced, or disregarded). Asset part: s 124-90 consequences (gain disregarded; replacement cost base reduced by the rolled-over amount). s 124-95(2): the market value of the other asset (when acquired) must exceed the part of the original asset cost base attributable to the new asset — a proportional attribution, different from the s 124-80(3) test.

statute.title: You receive both money and an asset

nodes.label: Roll-over applied — gain deferred into the replacement asset
nodes.body: The gain is reduced or disregarded under the relevant consequences and the replacement asset carries the adjusted cost base, preserving the gain until the replacement is later disposed of.

nodes.label: No roll-over — the CGT event is taxed in full
nodes.body: If you make a capital loss, receive no compensation, fail the replacement requirements or timing, or do not choose, the disposal or destruction is a normal CGT event and the gain or loss is recognised. CGT small business concessions (Division 152) may still be available for business assets.

nodes.label: Recapture events: CGT events J2, J5, J6 may later bring deferred gain to account
nodes.body: If you later dispose of the replacement asset, the deferred capital gain is recouped (CGT event A1 on the replacement asset — its first element of cost base is reduced by the rolled-over amount). CGT event J2 (share becomes redeemable, s 104-130) can also trigger recapture where the replacement is a share. J5 (s 104-175) and J6 (s 104-180) are not general later-disposal recapture events for this roll-over.
